<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard Python package build for `ww-manager`, a Wuthering Waves CLI Manager. The only source is a tarball fetched from the project's own GitHub repository at a specific tag (`v2.2.4`), with a real SHA256 checksum provided (not SKIP).

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, the following will occur:
1. The top-level PKGBUILD variables will be parsed — these are all standard metadata (pkgname, pkgver, depends, makedepends, source, sha256sums).
2. The source tarball will be downloaded from `https://github.com/timetetng/wutheringwaves-cli-manager/archive/refs/tags/v2.2.4.tar.gz` — the project's own upstream.
3. The tarball will be extracted, but nothing in `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` will execute.

There is no `pkgver()` function, no command substitution at the top level, no `eval`, no `base64 -d`, no `curl|bash` patterns, and no network requests to suspicious or unrelated destinations. The build and package functions use standard Python tooling (`python -m build`, `python -m installer`) which will not run during this gate.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>Standard PKGBUILD with verified upstream source, no risky top-level code.</summary>
</security_assessment>
